paragraphs.text:
Trembling with fear, you reel down the road from the Parthenon. 
You spy a lone figure ahead, a white-haired old man who uses 
a walking cane. You babble a warning in English, supposing 
that the alarm alone in your voice will be enough to dissuade 
him from going closer to the horrors lurking in the Parthenon 
behind you.
To your surprise, he answers in English. His voice is slow, but 
it inspires your confidence. “Fear no more,” he says. “Tonight the 
stars themselves bind those things to the top of the sacred hill. 
We have nothing to fear here.”
